STEP 1 - Scene: A side dish of roasted/pan-fried potato chunks, seasoned with what looks like herbs or spices, with a light oily sheen on the plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white square plate about 20 cm across (side-plate size). Area ≈ 3.14 × (10)² ≈ 314 cm² (square plate, slightly less, call it ~300 cm²).

STEP 3 - Items: Roasted potato pieces (about 7 chunks); a small amount of oil/seasoning residue on the plate.

STEP 4 - Area: Potato pieces cover roughly 20% of the plate (about 60 cm²). Oil residue is minor, under 2%. Total food coverage ~20%.

STEP 5 - Volume: 60 cm² × ~2 cm typical chunk height ≈ 120 ml gross volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut potato pieces are dense-ish, but the chunks are irregular with gaps; using bulk density ~0.6 g/ml for cut vegetables: 120 ml × 0.6 ≈ 72 g. Oil residue ~1 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Roasted potato ~150 kcal/100 g (cooked with some oil absorbed; plain boiled potato is ~87 kcal/100 g, roasted with fat is higher). Potato ≈ 72 g × 1.5 = 108 kcal. Oil ~1 g × 880 kcal/100 g ≈ 9 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Seven potato chunks covering about a fifth of a side plate, roughly 70 g, is plausible for a side portion of roasted potatoes. Total ~73 g, ~117 kcal.
